_comment: Adaptation to dynamics shifts on Hopper-v4, Ant-v4, Humanoid-v4: 18M steps per run, 3 seeds, no baselines
(the 24M run `trillium_dynamics_3env_24m.json` is the baseline: same seeds 18606, 16858, 63790, same hyperparameters).
20 experiments x 3 envs x 3 seeds = 180 runs on one 192-core node;
Two-segment runs switch at 9M; three-segment runs switch at 6M and 12M. The 24M base curves reach 90% of
their peak by ~6M (Ant), ~11M (Hopper), ~13M (Humanoid), so the Humanoid pre-shift policy is not fully converged.
Physics conditions use the same settings as the 24M baselines: moon gravity -1.62, gear_scale 2, friction_scale 0.3,
mass_scale 2. Scales are relative to the original model, so 1.0 restores the default; gravity -9.81 is Earth.
`moon_adapted` = Moon gravity + reward/termination changes. In the 24M run the mid termination bounds were the
only Moon variant that helped (Ant 1998 vs 1789, Hopper final 1419 vs 1183); removing or shrinking the healthy
reward collapsed learning on every env. Ant was the worst Moon env (37% of base), so it also gets a lower
control cost. Adapted settings: Hopper healthy_angle_range +-0.35 (default +-0.2); Ant healthy_z_range
[0.2, 1.5] (default [0.2, 1.0]) and ctrl_cost_weight 0.25 (default 0.5); Humanoid healthy_z_range [1.0, 2.75]
(default [1.0, 2.0]). Reward/termination kwargs set by a schedule stay until changed, so going back to base
spells out the defaults.
Groups: 1-7 base -> new world (4 single physics shifts, the adapted Moon, 2 compound shifts);
8-12 shifted world -> base; 13-20 three segments (there-and-back, adapt-after-the-fact, and chains of two
different physics shifts where the second replaces the first).
Videos: n_eval episodes every video_every steps, at each switch (just before it) and at the end.
Model snapshots every 1M steps and at the end.
